open_points.subject: API caller identity
open_points.text: “The credentials tell callers of the API apart” conflicts with “the one staff credential into each tool acting as staff — the operator, a frontend server.”
open_points.question: Must Registry distinguish individual staff callers and tools, or only distinguish the shared staff role from each named service?
options: One shared staff identity; distinguish only staff from named services
A separate credential and identity for every staff caller or tool
A shared credential for authorization plus another mechanism for caller identity
open_points.default_guess: Treat every holder of the shared staff credential as one staff identity and distinguish only that role from named services.

open_points.subject: Personal-data trust boundary
open_points.text: “Personal data — the customer's contact data (R0-06); readable by staff only” conflicts with “an agent passes whatever it reads — contact data, configuration, secrets — to the provider of the model the owner runs it on.”
open_points.question: Does “readable by staff only” constrain only Registry API authorization, or does it prohibit disclosure to model providers and other processors used by staff tools?
options: It describes only Registry API authorization; staff tools may transmit data under the owner's authority
Model providers are authorized processors inside the stated staff trust boundary
Contact data must not be transmitted to model providers
open_points.default_guess: Interpret staff-only as an API authorization rule and treat transmissions by an authorized staff tool as the owner's external disclosure.

open_points.subject: Unauthenticated callers on the host
open_points.text: “every unauthenticated read assumes the caller is inside” and “Everything that runs with the owner's access to Registry's host is the owner” do not classify an inside process that can reach loopback or the internal network but does not run with the owner's access.
open_points.question: Are all processes able to reach Registry's loopback or internal network trusted as the owner, including other host users or compromised workloads, or must deployment exclude such callers?
options: Assume a single-tenant host where every reachable process is owner-trusted
Require operating-system and network controls that restrict reachability to an enumerated set of owner-controlled processes
Authenticate reads because inside-but-untrusted callers may exist
open_points.default_guess: Assume deployment restricts reachability to owner-controlled processes and containers on a single-tenant host.

open_points.subject: Secret disclosure guarantee
open_points.text: “never in a record, a log line or an answer” does not identify which logging and response components are covered, while Registry may run behind servers or infrastructure that also produce logs and answers.
open_points.question: Which records, logs and responses are covered by the secret non-disclosure promise, and what observable behavior is required when a credential is received or rejected?
options: Only Registry-owned persistence, application logs and HTTP response bodies
All Registry deployment logs, including framework, access, proxy and container logs
All output produced anywhere on the host
open_points.default_guess: Cover Registry-owned persistence, application and access logs, and HTTP responses; never echo or log presented credentials.

open_points.subject: Credential generation
open_points.text: “The owner generates every secret” gives no required generation method, format, length or entropy and no failure for a weak or malformed configured secret.
open_points.question: What makes a staff credential or service token acceptable, and must Registry reject configuration containing a credential that does not meet that requirement?
options: Any non-empty owner-chosen opaque string is accepted
Credentials must satisfy specified format and entropy requirements that Registry validates at startup
Credentials must be generated by a named tool or procedure, while Registry treats them as opaque
open_points.default_guess: Require high-entropy opaque values generated outside Registry and validate a minimum length at startup.
